doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Manhattan Transfer Christmas album and Mandel's Christmas song
summary: Mandel describes working with Manhattan Transfer and his song that came out sounding like Christmas, which the Bergmans confirmed.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: [laughs] You did something – some of the credits you’ve been listed with lately have included what, well, the Manhattan Transfer Christmas album.
Oh yeah, that was fun. I loved doing that.
They’re a great group to work for, with.
For which you have a Christmas tune on there.
“All I Want for Christmas is You.”
Well, that isn’t the name of it, it’s called, “The Christmas Song.”
“A Christmas Love Song,” excuse me, “The Christmas Song,” is, “Chestnuts,” the Mel Tormé song.
Did you write it specifically for that recording?
No, no, I just wrote the song and it came out sounding like Christmas, I didn’t try to write a Christmas song.

I said for some reason this sounds like Christmas, I don’t know what makes a song sound like Christmas, I probably wrote it in July or something and took it to the Bergman’s and they said, “Yeah, that sounds like a Christmas song.” And then Marilyn said, “What makes it sound like a Christmas song?” And I says, “I really don’t know and I’m afraid if I try to figure it out how I did it I probably couldn’t do it again.”
